name: To-Do List
summary: A to-do list for each save, with tasks linked to towns, industries, lines and more
description:
A to-do list for each game, to keep track of what you want to build, fix or check next. A checklist button at the top left of the screen, next to the data layers button, opens the list. The + button adds a task at the top: type it and press Enter. Ticking a task moves it from the To Do tab to the Done tab; untick it to bring it back. Drag a task by its grip to reorder it (a blue bar shows where it will land, as with stops in the Line Manager), edit or delete it, and clear all done tasks at once with the bulldozer on the Done tab. The list and a data layer's legend window share their spot: opening one closes the other, and the legend opens a little lower, below the button.

Tasks can be about towns, industries, stations, lines and warehouses. Their windows get a To-Do card: how many open tasks are about this element, a + to start a new task about it, and a chain to add it to the task you clicked in the list. Click the card to expand it: the tasks about it, each with a tick box to mark it done and buttons to edit or delete it, so the list window is only needed for an overview; the done-tasks button in the card (a clipboard with a tick) adds the done tasks. In the list window, filter buttons show only the tasks about towns, industries, stations, lines or warehouses, and the eye shows only those about something on screen. Each linked element shows as a tag under the task's text: click it to go there and open its window. A tag greys out once its element is gone.

The list is saved with your game, so every save has its own. Removing the mod deletes the list from that save the next time it is loaded; nothing else of the mod stays in the save.

The list and the To-Do cards (with the list's filter buttons) can be turned off in the mod's Settings (the gear next to the mod when choosing a game's mods); the list stays in the save while they are off. Settings also has a Logging switch, off by default, that writes the mod's messages to the game log (stdout.txt) for bug reports.
